key_insight: QAOA has depth-dependent effective noise thresholds: deeper circuits generally require lower noise to maintain reliable approximation.
engineering_relevance: Thresholds can guide circuit-depth selection by distinguishing noise regimes where all, some, or no tested depths remain effective.
method: Run GPU-accelerated noisy QAOA simulations for MaxCut.
Fit approximation ratios with a generalised logistic surface.
Define effective noise thresholds using the surface’s inflection boundary.
evidence_signal: Evaluation covered three graph families with 6–18 vertices, depths up to 10, and three noise channels, with an additional assessment on ibm_marrakesh.
watch_item: Modelled gate errors understated observed hardware noise, so thresholds should guide qualitative depth selection rather than guarantee device performance.
paper_title: Effective Noise Thresholds for Reliable Quantum Approximation Optimisation Algorithm under Noisy Environment
